skills.name: Hegel property-based testing

skills.name: HeyGen MCP Server

skills.name: Higgsfield Skills

skills.name: HubSpot Sales Plugin

skills.name: Hugging Face MCP

skills.name: K-Dense Exploratory Data Analysis

skills.name: Kubernetes MCP Server

skills.name: Langfuse Skills

skills.name: Matt Pocock Diagnosing Bugs

skills.name: Matt Pocock TDD

skills.name: Supabase MCP Server

SKILL.md says version 1.1.1, January 2026. The skill changelog lists 1.6.0 on 2026-07-30.

The installer offers the whole pack, not this skill alone. You need a browser or app runtime to see the loaded model. No paid API or desktop modeler is listed. skills.name: Together AI Skills
skills.summary: One Together AI skill with guides and scripts for inference, fine-tuning, evaluations, batch jobs, media generation and GPUs.
skills.notes: A single together-ai skill routes to 15 domain guides with runnable Python v2 SDK and TypeScript scripts. Covers chat completions, batch inference, LoRA and full fine-tuning, LLM-as-a-judge evaluations, image, video and audio generation, sandboxes and GPU clusters. Needs TOGETHER_API_KEY; jobs bill your Together account. Also listed as togetherai-skills in claude-plugins-official.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Audit Context Building
skills.summary: Skill and workflow that map a codebase function by function before an audit, recording what each assumes, promises and depends on.
skills.notes: Version 2.0.2, by Omar Inuwa. Run /audit-context-building:audit-context <path>, or let the skill start it when an audit begins. Notes go to audit-context/functions/ and a summary to audit-context/DOSSIER.md. It reports no vulnerabilities and suggests no fixes, so pair it with a bug-hunting spell. The per-function fan-out uses Claude Code's Workflow tool. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add audit-context-building@trailofbits. Equippable in Claude Code trials.

skills.name: Trail of Bits fp-check
skills.summary: Skill that checks suspected security bugs one at a time and returns a true or false positive verdict with evidence after six gate reviews.
skills.notes: Version 1.0.5, by Maciej Domanski. Triggers when you ask whether a finding is real; it does not hunt for new bugs. Ships three agents (data-flow-analyzer, exploitability-verifier, poc-builder) and Stop and SubagentStop prompt hooks that block stopping until every bug has a verdict. The hooks match every stop, so trials flag the plugin and run it only with --allow-hazards. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add fp-check@trailofbits.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Insecure Defaults
skills.summary: Claude Code plugin that audits a repo, folder or file for fallback secrets, default credentials, fail-open switches and other insecure defaults.
skills.notes: Version 2.0.3. Run /insecure-defaults:audit with an optional path. The command starts a Claude Code workflow: one sweep agent per category greps for candidates, then verifier agents (Opus in the README) try to refute each one before it is reported. Ships a command and a workflow but no skill, so no Codex setup is documented. Equippable in Claude Code trials, where it needs the Workflow tool. For committed secrets the README suggests gitleaks or trufflehog. Audit only code you own or may review.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Mutation Testing
skills.summary: Skill that sets up mewt or muton mutation campaigns, sorts surviving mutants into test gaps or equivalents, and checks bugs they point to.
skills.notes: Version 1.9.2. Campaign setup needs mewt or muton and a runnable test suite. Analyzing saved results needs neither and accepts output from other mutation tools. The analysis writes mutation-testing-report.md with the tests to add but does not add them, and a bug counts as confirmed only after a reproduced proof of concept. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add mutation-testing@trailofbits. Equippable in Claude Code trials; campaigns there need mewt or muton already installed.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Property-Based Testing
skills.summary: Skill that writes, reviews and triages property-based tests with Hypothesis, fast-check, proptest, and Echidna or Medusa for Solidity.
skills.notes: Version 1.2.2, by Henrik Brodin. Suits code with a clear rule to test: encode and decode pairs, parsers, normalizers, validators, data structures and contract state invariants. Not for coverage-guided fuzzing. It leaves adding a test library to you, so trials pass only where Hypothesis, fast-check or a similar library is already installed. Manual install: /plugin install trailofbits/skills/plugins/property-based-testing. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add property-based-testing@trailofbits.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Sharp Edges
skills.summary: Skill and agent that find error-prone APIs, dangerous configuration options and footgun designs that make security mistakes easy.
skills.notes: Version 1.1.3. Reviews code and designs from three viewpoints: a malicious developer, a lazy one who copies the first example, and a confused one who swaps parameters. The skill only reads files (Read, Grep, Glob); the sharp-edges-analyzer agent runs the same analysis in its own context. Findings are design risks without an exploit. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add sharp-edges@trailofbits. Equippable in Claude Code trials and needs no network.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Skills
skills.summary: Trail of Bits marketplace of security plugins for code audits, Semgrep and CodeQL, smart contracts and variant analysis.
skills.notes: A marketplace of 46 plugins that you install one by one. Security picks include audit-context-building, differential-review, insecure-defaults, sharp-edges, static-analysis, variant-analysis, supply-chain-risk-auditor and building-secure-contracts. Codex reads the same marketplace: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add <plugin-name>@trailofbits. Some plugins are not security tools, such as let-fate-decide and culture-index. Audit only code you own or are authorized to review.

skills.name: Trail of Bits Variant Analysis
skills.summary: Skill and workflow that take one known bug, extract its root cause and hunt the other places it occurs, with CodeQL and Semgrep templates.
skills.notes: Version 2.0.4, by Axel Mierczuk. Starts from a bug you already found; the skill says it is not for initial discovery. /variant-analysis:variants runs a Claude Code workflow with one subagent per expansion axis, and below about 40 source files it does a single narrow sweep. Templates cover Python, JavaScript, Java, Go and C++. Codex: codex plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills, then codex plugin add variant-analysis@trailofbits. Equippable in Claude Code trials; the Semgrep and CodeQL steps need those tools installed.

skills.name: Trunk Flaky Tests
skills.summary: Claude Code plugin with a flaky test patterns skill, plus Trunk commands that explain and fix flaky tests from your CI history.
skills.install:
claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-community
claude plugin install trunk@claude-community
skills.notes: The /trunk:fix-flaky, /trunk:why-flaky and /trunk:setup-uploads commands call the Trunk MCP server, which needs a Trunk account (OAuth sign in) and test results uploaded from CI. Without that, only the flaky-test-patterns skill helps: it maps symptoms such as sleeps, clock use, shared state, real network calls and fixed ports to fixes. In a sealed trial arena the MCP part cannot connect, and its .mcp.json means trials need --allow-hazards. A trunk-ci-setup skill covers CI upload config.

skills.name: UI UX Pro Max
skills.summary: Searches a local catalog of UI styles, palettes, type pairings, UX guidelines, icons, and stack patterns.
skills.install:
npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli
uipro init --ai claude
uipro init --ai codex
skills.notes: Needs Python 3.x; the search script uses the standard library only and makes no network calls. The npm package is ui-ux-pro-max-cli; older uipro-cli releases are stale. Claude Code alternative: /plugin marketplace add nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill then /plugin install ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill. Run uipro init in the project. The skill installs nothing for you. If project files do not show a stack, the agent asks instead of assuming one. An empty search is retried once, then labeled as built-in defaults. Results are recommendations.

skills.name: Unreal Engine Skills for Claude Code
skills.summary: Official Claude Code plugin that drives a running Unreal Editor through MCP toolsets.
skills.notes: Needs Unreal Editor running with ModelContextProtocol and AllToolsets enabled, then ModelContextProtocol.StartServer. Default port is 8000. The session hook needs bash on PATH (macOS, Linux, or Windows via Git Bash or WSL). Claude Code only. Tools can change live project files, including through Python.

skills.name: Vercel MCP
skills.summary: Reads Vercel docs, projects, deployments, logs, and Web Analytics after you sign in.
skills.notes: Remote server at https://mcp.vercel.com. OAuth. Available on all plans under Vercel's AI Product Terms. Only clients Vercel has approved can connect. Tools depend on the grant and your team role. Docs page updated 2026-09-15. No SPDX license is published for the hosted service.

skills.name: Vercel React Best Practices
skills.summary: React and Next.js rules for waterfalls, bundle size, server work, and re-renders.
skills.notes: npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills installs the skills in that repo, not this file alone. The skill lists rules in eight groups, led by waterfall removal and bundle size. Read the matching rules file before applying one. It does not run a profiler or edit code by itself. MIT is declared in SKILL.md; the repo has no LICENSE file.

skills.name: Vercel React Native Skills
skills.summary: React Native and Expo rules for lists, animation, navigation, images, and native modules.
skills.notes: Rules for React Native and Expo, highest priority first: FlashList and list item cost, then Reanimated (transform and opacity only), native stack and tabs, expo-image, and monorepo native deps. The installer adds every skill in vercel-labs/agent-skills. Frontmatter name is vercel-react-native-skills; the folder is react-native-skills. MIT is declared in SKILL.md; the repo has no LICENSE file.

skills.name: Vercel Web Design Guidelines
skills.summary: Fetches Vercel's interface rules and reports UI findings as file:line notes.
skills.notes: Same installer as the other skills in vercel-labs/agent-skills. Before each review it fetches the guidelines from vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines, so it needs network. If you do not name files, it asks which files to review. Output is the file:line format from those rules. No license is declared: the repo has no LICENSE file and this SKILL.md names none.

skills.name: Vercel Writing Guidelines
skills.summary: Fetches Vercel's writing rules and reviews docs, returning file and line findings.
skills.notes: The installer adds every skill in vercel-labs/agent-skills. Each review fetches current rules from vercel-labs/writing-guidelines, so it needs network access. Output is file:line findings. Ask it to review docs, writing style, or voice.

skills.name: Weights & Biases MCP
skills.summary: Queries W&B runs and Weave traces, compares and diagnoses runs, summarizes evals and writes W&B reports.
skills.install: claude mcp add --transport http wandb https://mcp.withwandb.com/mcp --scope user --header "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key-here>"
skills.notes: Hosted at https://mcp.withwandb.com/mcp with your W&B API key; a local server also exists. Tools include query_weave_traces_tool, query_wandb_tool, compare_runs_tool, diagnose_run_tool, summarize_evaluation_tool and create_wandb_report_tool. log_analysis_to_wandb and report creation write to your account; tool profiles and a read-only mode can limit that. Codex install sets WANDB_API_KEY first.

skills.name: Windmill MCP
skills.summary: Official Windmill MCP to run scripts and flows and manage jobs, resources and schedules.
skills.notes: Needs a Windmill Cloud or self-hosted workspace. OAuth gateway is <base_url>/api/mcp/gateway. The Claude Code command in the docs uses a token URL. Token URLs can land in history and logs. A superadmin can refuse ?token= and force OAuth or a Bearer header. Folder scope limits which scripts and flows appear. No Codex setup is documented.

skills.name: Unit Testing (wshobson agents)
skills.summary: Claude Code plugin with a test-generate command plus test automator and debugger subagents for Python and JavaScript unit tests.
skills.notes: /unit-testing:test-generate writes pytest, Jest or React component tests with mocks and edge cases, then checks coverage gaps. The unit-testing-debugger agent captures the error, reproduces it, isolates the failure and makes a minimal fix. The test-automator agent's prompt is broad and names cloud and browser tools, so point it at local runners. No hooks or MCP, so trials equip it as is. It has no skills, so the native Codex install adds nothing from it.

skills.name: Zapier MCP
skills.summary: Hosted Zapier MCP for actions in connected apps, such as send, update and lookup.
skills.notes: Sign in during setup. No local app. These clients should not create a server at mcp.zapier.com first. A Team or Enterprise Claude org may need Owner approval before you can add MCP servers. Each successful call uses two Zapier tasks. Failed calls do not. On WSL, the OAuth callback may never return. Use a native Windows or macOS terminal. Zapier also publishes a Claude Code plugin: zapier@claude-plugins-official.

workflows.name: Build a Claude agent, then trace and grade it

steps.note: Scaffolds and verifies a Claude Agent SDK app.
Adds MLflow tracing, then builds scorers and runs an evaluation.

workflows.why: The Agent SDK plugin gets a working, verified starter agent. MLflow skills then add tracing (Anthropic is a supported library) and an evaluation, so changes to the agent can be measured instead of guessed.

workflows.name: Python CAD model, checked for printing

steps.note: Builds the model in Python with build123d and exports it as an STL file.
Measures the exported mesh and checks whether it will print.

workflows.why: Build the model in build123d and export it as STL, then use OpenSCAD MCP to measure the exported mesh and check that it will print. Only the exported file passes between them; the parametric history stays in build123d.

workflows.name: Terraform plan to watched AWS deploy

steps.note: Looks up current provider and module docs so the HCL uses real arguments.
Builds and deploys the service on AWS with the AWS MCP Server.
Checks logs, traces and monitors for the new service after the deploy.

workflows.why: Write infrastructure from current docs, deploy it, then confirm it is healthy from real telemetry. Each step needs its own account: HCP Terraform is optional, AWS and Datadog are not.

workflows.name: Word draft with a PDF check

steps.note: Drafts the content with you: gathers context, refines the text and tests it on a reader.
Creates the Word document from the draft, including its formatting.
Reads the exported PDF so you can check the result.

workflows.why: Write the content first, turn it into a Word document, then check the PDF exported from it. Use an authorized Anthropic route, and sort out the license limits before you copy any of these skill files.

workflows.name: Notion notes to a reviewed draft

steps.note: Reads the Notion pages you have authorized for background material.
Structures the document and tests whether a reader can follow it.
Checks the prose against Vercel's fetched writing rules and reports findings by file and line.

workflows.why: Pull in the workspace context you are authorized to use, shape the document and test it on a reader, then check the prose against a set of written rules.

workflows.name: Analyze local files, then check the result

steps.note: Runs DuckDB SQL on local files or an in-memory database.
Profiles the data, charts the answer and validates it before you share.

workflows.why: DuckDB gives the agent a SQL engine for local files with no warehouse account. The Data plugin then profiles the results, draws the chart and runs its validation pass before anyone sees the numbers.

workflows.name: Generated image, sized for every slot

steps.note: Generates the image after you see and approve the estimated cost.
Uploads the image and writes transformation URLs for each size and crop.

workflows.why: fal makes the image and returns a download link. Cloudinary stores that file and serves resized and cropped versions through transformation URLs, so one generated image covers every placement.

workflows.name: Figma design to a tested interface

steps.note: Reads the source design from Figma, including its variables and components.
Guides the visual build: typography, layout and a deliberate look.
Reviews the UI code against Vercel's interface guidelines and reports findings by file and line.
Drives a real browser to test the interactions, using accessibility snapshots.

workflows.why: Read the source design, build the visuals on purpose, and check the UI against interface rules. Finish by testing the real interactions so you aren't judging the result from screenshots alone.

workflows.name: shadcn components with registry tools

steps.note: Looks at your project and guides which components to use, how to combine them and how to customize them.
Browses, searches and installs components from shadcn-compatible registries.

workflows.why: The skill explains how to find components through MCP, and the server provides the tools to browse, search and install them from registries.

workflows.name: Guided build of a database feature

steps.note: Walks the feature through seven phases, from exploring the code to architecture, build and review.
Applies Postgres rules for schema, SQL, RLS, indexes and performance.
Connects to a scoped development project so you can inspect the database.
Runs the finished feature in a real browser to check the flow.

workflows.why: Follow a guided build, apply Postgres rules to the database work, and inspect a scoped development project. Then run the finished flow in a browser.

workflows.name: Next.js app from dev to deploy

steps.note: Gives React and Next.js guidance on data fetching, rendering and bundle size.
Reads runtime errors, routes and logs from the running Next.js 16+ dev server.
Checks the deployment on Vercel, along with its logs.
Pulls in the pull request and repository context.

workflows.why: Each spell covers a different stage: React and Next.js guidance while you write, runtime diagnostics from the local dev server, the deployed state on Vercel and the pull request on GitHub.

workflows.name: Avatar clip inside a captioned video

steps.note: Renders the talking avatar clip from your script.
Adds titles, captions and music around the clip and renders the MP4.

workflows.why: HeyGen makes the avatar footage. HyperFrames places that clip in an HTML composition with captions and titles, then renders the final MP4 on your machine.

workflows.name: Build Make scenarios with guidance

steps.note: Runs and manages your Make scenarios in the cloud. The management tools need a paid plan.
Adds Make's official scenario guidance and can register the MCP server.

workflows.why: Make's official scenario guidance shows how to find, configure and run scenarios with Make MCP. The plugin can also register the server for you.

workflows.name: Keyword research to measured page

steps.note: Finds keywords and the pages that rank for them.
Drafts the page and checks it against your brand voice.
Reads traffic and events for the page once it is live.

workflows.why: Pick a target from search data, write for it, then measure the result instead of guessing. Ahrefs needs a paid plan and Google Analytics needs a Cloud project with credentials.

workflows.name: Meeting recording to a Spotify recap

steps.note: Transcribes the meeting recording.
Turns the transcript into a short narrated recap and uploads it.

workflows.why: Deepgram turns the recording into a transcript. Save to Spotify lists meeting recaps from a transcript as one of its uses: it writes a short summary, narrates it and saves the episode to Spotify.

workflows.name: Meshy assets in a Blender scene

steps.note: Generates the 3D assets and downloads them as GLB files. Generation uses credits.
Imports the GLB into Blender to place, light, inspect and render the scene.

workflows.why: Generate and download assets with Meshy, then import the GLB files into Blender to place them in a scene, light it, inspect it and render it.

workflows.name: Generated model on a web page

steps.note: Generates the model with the Meshy CLI and downloads it as a GLB. Cloud runs use credits.
Loads the GLB in the browser with loading progress, an environment and proper disposal.

workflows.why: Meshy's CLI guidance generates the GLB and delivers it. Three.js guidance then covers loading it in the browser, with a progress display, environment setup and disposal when it's no longer needed.

workflows.name: Navigation for an Expo app

steps.note: Sets the shared project rules and picks the SDK version, then hands navigation to expo-router.
Builds the navigation: file routes, stacks, tabs, links, modals and headers.

workflows.why: The Expo overview sends navigation tasks straight to expo-router and supplies the shared setup and SDK selection rules.

workflows.name: Upgrade Expo, then check in CI

steps.note: Sets the shared project rules and picks the right SDK version.
Guides the SDK upgrade and dependency fixes for your exact version.
Runs the upgraded app through your EAS pipelines. EAS use can cost money.

workflows.why: Follow upgrade guidance written for your SDK version, then check the upgraded app in your EAS pipelines. Be clear up front about what the EAS services will cost.

workflows.name: Build n8n workflows with community tools

steps.note: Looks up node docs and templates, validates workflows and can manage live ones. Telemetry is on by default.
Explains which tool to use, how to format node parameters and how to validate the workflow.

workflows.why: The community server finds nodes and works on workflows. Its matching skill explains which tool to pick, how to format parameters and how to validate the result.

workflows.name: Build n8n workflows with official tools

steps.note: Finds, builds, edits, tests and runs workflows on your n8n instance.
Adds n8n's official skills and hooks. In Claude it also registers the server, so don't add another.

workflows.why: n8n's official skills and hooks are made to guide its official instance tools. The Claude plugin can register the server on its own, so don't add a second connection.

workflows.name: Design in OpenSCAD by measurement

steps.note: Guides the parametric design and says what to check: numbers, measurements and the assembly.
Renders, measures, checks the assembly and exports the model.

workflows.why: The skill has you check syntax, take measurements, verify assemblies and export through the matching MCP tools before you trust how the render looks.

workflows.name: Check the papers, then the latest news

steps.note: Finds peer-reviewed papers with citations.
Adds recent web sources the papers may not cover yet.

workflows.why: Consensus covers published research with citations. Perplexity search fills in recent web sources, so the answer shows both the evidence base and what changed since.

workflows.name: Plain language pass

steps.note: Rewrite the draft without changing its claims.
Check the rewrite against the fetched writing rules.

workflows.why: Strip AI phrasing from a draft, then check the rewrite against Vercel's writing rules.

workflows.name: Make a video, then export versions

steps.note: Builds the video as a React composition with animation, captions and media.
Normalizes source media and makes compressed, resized or subtitled delivery files.

workflows.why: Build the composition in Remotion, then use FFmpeg recipes to normalize the source media and produce compressed, resized or subtitled files for delivery.

workflows.name: Edit in DaVinci Resolve with guidance

steps.note: Runs Resolve actions on timelines, media, Fusion, grading and render jobs.
Explains object ID chaining, Fusion wiring and recipes that go from edit to render.

workflows.why: The server carries out actions in Resolve. The companion skill explains how to chain object IDs, wire Fusion nodes and take an edit all the way to render.

workflows.name: Review React code and UI

steps.note: Reviews the change for defects and project rule breaks, reporting only high-confidence findings.
Checks rendering, data fetching and bundle size for React performance problems.
Checks the UI code against Vercel's interface guidelines and reports findings by file and line.

workflows.why: A general review catches defects and broken project rules. Two focused guides then add checks for React performance and UI implementation.

workflows.name: A second opinion on your PR

steps.note: Pulls in the repository and pull request context.
Runs a separate CodeRabbit review. Get human approval before comments, fixes or paid operations.

workflows.why: GitHub supplies the repository and pull request context, and CodeRabbit gives a separate review. A person should still approve comments, fixes and paid operations.

workflows.name: Spline scene for your website

steps.note: Builds and inspects the editable scene in the running Spline desktop app.
Embeds the scene from its real exported URL and adds the attribution the source requires.

workflows.why: Build an editable scene through the desktop MCP and get the real URL the editor exports. Then add the scene to your site with the documented web packages and the required attribution.

workflows.name: Support ticket to filed bug

steps.note: Finds the conversations and the customer's history.
Triages the issue, drafts the reply and writes the escalation.
Files the escalation as a Linear issue for engineering.

workflows.why: Read what customers report, answer them, and hand real bugs to engineering with repro steps attached. The Intercom plugin is read-only, so replies are sent from Intercom by a person.

workflows.name: Test-first bug hunt

steps.note: Reproduce the failure and keep the evidence.
Write the failing check, then the smallest fix.

workflows.why: Reproduce the failure first, then lock the repair behind a test that failed before the fix.

workflows.name: Reproduce a reported error

steps.note: Pulls the reported errors, traces and project context from Sentry.
Gathers evidence and reproduces the failure to find the root cause before any fix.
Runs the same browser flow again after the fix to confirm it works.

workflows.why: Tie the reported errors to a browser flow you can repeat, find the root cause, then run the same flow again after the fix.

workflows.name: Pin the bug, watch it live

steps.note: Writes the regression test first, through public interfaces, one behavior at a time.
Exercises the UI with Python Playwright scripts against your local app.
Inspects console, network and performance evidence in Chrome, after the other browser is done.

workflows.why: Write a test that pins the behavior, exercise the UI, then read the runtime evidence. Use the browser tools one at a time instead of running competing browser instances.
